claims.text: The GPS trace establishes a route deviation on this trip: the trace distance is 19.12 km against a booked optimal of 14.4 km, an excess of 4.72 km, which is 32.78% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass — the excess exceeds 20% of optimal and exceeds 0.8 km absolute. The governing field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 19.1 km.

The rider has discharged the initial burden under POL-RD-08: the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-02857 and the trace runs from the recorded trip_started timestamp 2026-09-09T22:06:33+08:00 to trip_completed 22:31:33+08:00, matching the trip record. The excess of 4.72 km / 32.78% meets the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired trace (100% coverage, 10 s sampling, no gaps). The burden therefore shifts to the driver.

The driver's only explanation is the one-word counterparty statement 'Traffic.' No traffic_advisory covering this trip window is on file — EV-ADVIS-02857-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and its issue detail states no advisory covers the Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 corridor in this window. Under POL-RD-13 the assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory and nothing else; with no advisory the comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The driver names no evidence ID for any advisory, so this is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation.

No rider-requested detour can excuse the excess: the chat log for this trip contains zero messages (message_count 0, no waypoint_hint, no road named), so POL-RD-04(a)-(c) cannot be met and the corroboration test cannot even be run. The driver has pointed to no chat instruction, and none exists on the record.

No relocation of the pickup or dropoff point occurred: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 does not apply and the booked optimal of 14.4 km stands as the baseline.

The trip is not a pooled trip: vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-12 does not apply and the matched-itinerary baseline does not displace the booked optimal.

The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 runs. Charged total is 25.93. Recomputed fare on the booked optimal route = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 14.4 + 0.28 x 19.4) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP/tolls + 0 fixed surcharges + 0 waiting time - 0 promo = (3.80 + 10.80 + 5.432) + 0.80 = 20.832. Refund = 25.93 - 20.832 = 5.098, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 5.10. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 5.10.

The rider's claim text asserts 'six deviation flags' and demands a full refund. The six is driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags, a LIFETIME counter, which POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 expressly forbid as the basis of the pattern test; the trailing-90-day figure is driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d = 0, and 0/260 completed trips is far below the 0.05 ratio. No repeat-deviation pattern is established, so no POL-RD-06(b) full-refund uplift is available and the remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial only. I do not press the full-refund claim.

No ERP or toll lines are charged (tolls_erp 0.0, erp_gantries empty, off-route and on-route ERP totals both 0.00) and no airport surcharge applies, so there is no standalone pass-through correction to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. Under POL-RD-09(1) any off-route ERP would already be comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund and must never be added twice.

The GPS trace is clean for policy purposes: 100% coverage, 151 fixes at a 10 s interval, max_gap_sec 0.0 and no gaps, so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) is not engaged and no independent corroboration is required. The deviation stands on the trace alone.

claims.text: The rider's claim that this driver 'has six deviation flags' is built on driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags, a LIFETIME counter. The clause that governs repeat-deviation conduct, POL-RD-06, names driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d, and that field is 0. POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting the lifetime counter for the trailing-window counter, so the rider's stated ground of decision is discarded and cannot support any adverse finding against the driver.

Even on the rider's own arithmetic the repeat-pattern test fails: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 260, so the ratio is 0.000, far below the 0.05 threshold, and the flag count is below the 3 required. No pattern is established and no POL-RD-06 uplift, balance-tilt or conduct referral is available on this record.

The driver's explanation for the extra distance is 'Traffic.' That is a general assertion of bad traffic. POL-RD-08 requires the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause, and a general assertion unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID does not discharge the burden. The counterparty_statement cites no evidence ID at all, so under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight.

No traffic advisory covers this trip window: EV-ADVIS-02857-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT. Under POL-RD-13 the driver's traffic assertion cannot be tested against any advisory, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal route. The deviation therefore stands at the measured figure.

The excess is measured on the governing field. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the field that governs, and it is 19.12 km against an optimal of 14.4 km, an excess of 4.72 km and 32.78 percent. Both establishment tests pass: 4.72 km exceeds the 0.8 km absolute threshold and 32.78 percent exceeds the 20 percent threshold. The deviation is ESTABLISHED.

The excess does not reach the materiality gate, which is the driver's strongest point on the finding. POL-RD-01 sets materiality at more than 50 percent of optimal or more than 8.0 km absolute; the measured excess is 32.78 percent and 4.72 km, so neither limb is met. The deviation is established but not MATERIAL, and the POL-RD-06 profile check is not triggered by materiality.

The trace is clean and unimpaired for policy purposes, so the rider's excess is proven on the trace alone and no corroboration is needed. POL-RD-07 impairs a trace only on a gap over 90 seconds, a jump over 500 m, or a sustained interval above 30 seconds; this trace has 151 fixes at a 10 second interval, 100 percent coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. The admissibility pre-pass agrees, tagging EV-GPS-02857 COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

The rider's burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged: the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-02857 and the trace runs from the recorded trip_started timestamp 2026-09-09T22:06:33+08:00 to trip_completed 2026-09-09T22:31:33+08:00, matching the trip record. The excess is measured from an unimpaired trace, so the burden shifts to the driver, who has pointed to no artifact and no clause.

No rider-requested detour can excuse any part of the excess. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log, and the chat log for this trip holds zero messages with no first or last message timestamp. There is no instruction to corroborate, so no distance is excluded and the excess stands as measured.

No relocation of the pickup or dropoff point can excuse the excess. POL-RD-05 requires a non-null pickup_amended_at or dropoff_amended_at, and both are null on the trip record, as are amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min. The booked optimal of 14.4 km is therefore the correct baseline and no re-quote is available to the driver.

The pooled-trip baseline does not apply. POL-RD-12 governs only where trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_POOL; this trip is RYDE_X and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so the matched-itinerary baseline is unavailable and the booked optimal of 14.4 km governs under POL-RD-01.

The fare is METERED, so the POL-RD-02 recomputation runs and the rider is entitled to the arithmetic refund. The recomputed fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 14.4 + 0.28 x 19.4) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 20.8320, against a charged_total of 25.93, giving a refund of 5.0980, rounded up to SGD 5.10. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and below the 90 percent full-refund share, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND.

The rider's demand for a full refund is not supported and should be rejected. The refund reaches only 19.66 percent of charged_total, well short of the 90 percent full_refund_share POL-RD-02 requires, and the rider's only stated ground - six deviation flags - is the lifetime counter POL-GEN-01 forbids. The rider is entitled to the SGD 5.10 partial refund and no more.

No ERP or surcharge correction is due to the rider. The fare breakdown carries zero ERP gantries and zero tolls, and the airport surcharge is 0.0 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. POL-RD-09 therefore adds nothing on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, and the anti-double-count rule in POL-RD-09(1) is not engaged.

No driver compensation is available on this record. POL-RD-04's compensation limb requires the fare_breakdown to show the rider was billed for less distance than the gps_trace records by more than 1.0 km; here the billed distance is 19.1 km against a trace of 19.12 km, a shortfall of 0.02 km, far below the 1.0 km gate. The driver is owed nothing under that limb.

The rider's own profile does not weaken the claim. POL-RD-08's corroboration uplift applies only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1 or fewer; this rider has 1 claim and 0 substantiated, so the count limb is not met and no extra corroboration beyond the trace is required. The claim is proven on the trace alone.

The driver's own profile is context only and cannot ground a finding either way. POL-GEN-01 permits only deviation_flags_90d and completed_trips_90d to be cited for the POL-RD-06 test, and both are addressed above; the driver's rating, acceptance rate, cancellation rate, lifetime_trips and prior_deviation_flags are CONTEXT ONLY and may not carry an adverse finding against him. The rider's reliance on the lifetime flag count is discarded on that footing.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling is addressed to both parties. The claim is partly upheld: the rider is refunded SGD 5.10 of the SGD 25.93 charged, and no more.

THE DEVIATION IS PROVEN, BUT NOT MATERIAL. The governing measurement is gps_trace.trace_distance_km on EV-GPS-02857 (POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern over the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 19.1 km). The trace is 19.12 km against a booked optimal of 14.4 km (EV-TRIP-02857): an excess of 4.72 km, or 32.78% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (4.72 km > 0.8 km; 32.78% > 20%), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is not MATERIAL: the excess is below the 50% and 8.0 km materiality gates, so the POL-RD-06 profile check is not triggered by materiality.

NO EXCUSE DISPLACES THE EXCESS. The driver's counterparty statement ('Traffic.') names no evidence ID, and no traffic advisory covers this trip window (EV-ADVIS-02857-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT). Under POL-RD-13 the assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory and nothing else; with no advisory the comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. It neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal. The chat log (EV-CHAT-02857) holds zero messages, so no rider-requested detour exists under POL-RD-04. No pickup/dropoff amendment exists under POL-RD-05 (both timestamps and amended_optimal_distance_km are null), and the trip is RYDE_X, not pooled, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. The booked optimal of 14.4 km is the correct baseline.

REMEDY (POL-RD-02, METERED fare). charged_total = 25.93 (EV-FARE-02857). recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 14.4 + 0.28 x 19.4) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP/tolls + 0 fixed surcharges + 0 waiting time - 0 promo = 20.832. Refund = 25.93 - 20.832 = 5.098, rounded up to SGD 5.10. ledger.claim: No traffic advisory covers this trip window: EV-ADVIS-02857-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT. Under POL-RD-13 the driver's traffic assertion cannot be tested against any advisory, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal route. The deviation therefore stands at the measured figure.

The excess is measured on the governing field. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the field that governs, and it is 19.12 km against an optimal of 14.4 km, an excess of 4.72 km and 32.78 percent. Both establishment tests pass: 4.72 km exceeds the 0.8 km absolute threshold and 32.78 percent exceeds the 20 percent threshold. The deviation is ESTABLISHED.

The excess does not reach the materiality gate, which is the driver's strongest point on the finding. POL-RD-01 sets materiality at more than 50 percent of optimal or more than 8.0 km absolute; the measured excess is 32.78 percent and 4.72 km, so neither limb is met. The deviation is established but not MATERIAL, and the POL-RD-06 profile check is not triggered by materiality.

The trace is clean and unimpaired for policy purposes, so the rider's excess is proven on the trace alone and no corroboration is needed. POL-RD-07 impairs a trace only on a gap over 90 seconds, a jump over 500 m, or a sustained interval above 30 seconds; this trace has 151 fixes at a 10 second interval, 100 percent coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. The admissibility pre-pass agrees, tagging EV-GPS-02857 COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

The rider's burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged: the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-02857 and the trace runs from the recorded trip_started timestamp 2026-09-09T22:06:33+08:00 to trip_completed 2026-09-09T22:31:33+08:00, matching the trip record. The excess is measured from an unimpaired trace, so the burden shifts to the driver, who has pointed to no artifact and no clause.

No rider-requested detour can excuse any part of the excess. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log, and the chat log for this trip holds zero messages with no first or last message timestamp. There is no instruction to corroborate, so no distance is excluded and the excess stands as measured.

No relocation of the pickup or dropoff point can excuse the excess. POL-RD-05 requires a non-null pickup_amended_at or dropoff_amended_at, and both are null on the trip record, as are amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min. The booked optimal of 14.4 km is therefore the correct baseline and no re-quote is available to the driver.

The pooled-trip baseline does not apply. POL-RD-12 governs only where trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_POOL; this trip is RYDE_X and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so the matched-itinerary baseline is unavailable and the booked optimal of 14.4 km governs under POL-RD-01.

The fare is METERED, so the POL-RD-02 recomputation runs and the rider is entitled to the arithmetic refund. The recomputed fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 14.4 + 0.28 x 19.4) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 20.8320, against a charged_total of 25.93, giving a refund of 5.0980, rounded up to SGD 5.10. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and below the 90 percent full-refund share, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND.

The rider's demand for a full refund is not supported and should be rejected. The refund reaches only 19.66 percent of charged_total, well short of the 90 percent full_refund_share POL-RD-02 requires, and the rider's only stated ground - six deviation flags - is the lifetime counter POL-GEN-01 forbids. The rider is entitled to the SGD 5.10 partial refund and no more.

No ERP or surcharge correction is due to the rider. The fare breakdown carries zero ERP gantries and zero tolls, and the airport surcharge is 0.0 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. POL-RD-09 therefore adds nothing on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, and the anti-double-count rule in POL-RD-09(1) is not engaged.

No driver compensation is available on this record. POL-RD-04's compensation limb requires the fare_breakdown to show the rider was billed for less distance than the gps_trace records by more than 1.0 km; here the billed distance is 19.1 km against a trace of 19.12 km, a shortfall of 0.02 km, far below the 1.0 km gate. The driver is owed nothing under that limb.

The rider's own profile does not weaken the claim. POL-RD-08's corroboration uplift applies only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1 or fewer; this rider has 1 claim and 0 substantiated, so the count limb is not met and no extra corroboration beyond the trace is required. The claim is proven on the trace alone.

The driver's own profile is context only and cannot ground a finding either way. POL-GEN-01 permits only deviation_flags_90d and completed_trips_90d to be cited for the POL-RD-06 test, and both are addressed above; the driver's rating, acceptance rate, cancellation rate, lifetime_trips and prior_deviation_flags are CONTEXT ONLY and may not carry an adverse finding against him. The rider's reliance on the lifetime flag count is discarded on that footing.
